title: Choose the landing page's structure
question: Colours, fonts and the game stay. Which structure should the page around them take?

options.label: Two stages
options.thesis: The page is two playable stages: the review you live through, then the real map of it.
options.viewport: Headline left and subhead with Play a review right, then the game in a full-width hood with its green progress bar.
options.risk: Little text between stages, so each surviving sentence must be set large to carry its weight.

options.label: Story panel
options.thesis: The page takes the viewer's own layout: a story panel on the left, the canvas on the right.
options.viewport: A white panel holds the headline, subhead, action and the page's section list; the game fills the canvas beside it, later swapped for the live map.
options.risk: A sticky two-pane page is the most engineering, and on phones it stacks into a plain column.

options.label: Diff wall
options.thesis: A muted wall of the real #8613 diff runs down the page's edge and ends where the live map begins.
options.viewport: A pale diff gutter on the left, the headline and action beside it, and the top of the game below.
options.risk: The gutter can read as decoration or noise if it is not kept quiet.
